headline: RU student Chesi Tripura dies after road accident
summary: The Microbiology student was flown to Dhaka via air ambulance for advanced treatment but succumbed to her injuries on Thursday night.
details: Chesi Tripura, a student of the 2021-22 session of the Microbiology Department at Rajshahi University (RU), has passed away following a severe road accident.
She died on Thursday night around 11 PM while undergoing treatment at the National Institute of Neurosciences and Hospital in Dhaka.
The death was confirmed by the university's proctor, Professor Mahbubur Rahman, who was present at the hospital.

The accident occurred last Monday evening in the Durgapur area while Chesi and a classmate were returning to campus in a CNG-powered auto-rickshaw after attending a Puja invitation at a classmate's home in Bagmara.
A speeding truck hit the auto-rickshaw, causing Chesi to sustain severe head injuries.
She was initially taken to the Durgapur Upazila Health Complex and then transferred to Rajshahi Medical College (RAMC) Hospital, where she was later moved to the ICU.
Due to the need for advanced medical care, the university authorities arranged for her to be transported to Dhaka via air ambulance on Tuesday afternoon.
Despite these efforts, she passed away on Thursday night while receiving treatment in the capital.
caption:
A Rajshahi University student has died after a severe road accident, despite being flown to Dhaka via air ambulance for emergency care.

Chesi Tripura, a student of the 2021-22 session of the Microbiology Department at Rajshahi University (RU), has passed away following a severe road accident.

She died on Thursday night around 11 PM while undergoing treatment at the National Institute of Neurosciences and Hospital in Dhaka.

The death was confirmed by the university's proctor, Professor Mahbubur Rahman, who was present at the hospital.

The accident occurred last Monday evening in the Durgapur area while Chesi and a classmate were returning to campus in a CNG-powered auto-rickshaw after attending a Puja invitation at a classmate's home in Bagmara.

A speeding truck hit the auto-rickshaw, causing Chesi to sustain severe head injuries.

She was initially taken to the Durgapur Upazila Health Complex and then transferred to Rajshahi Medical College (RAMC) Hospital, where she was later moved to the ICU.

Due to the need for advanced medical care, the university authorities arranged for her to be transported to Dhaka via air ambulance on Tuesday afternoon.

Despite these efforts, she passed away on Thursday night while receiving treatment in the capital.

headline_marked: Japan to arrange [[$6.36bn private investment]] in Bangladesh
headline: Japan to arrange $6.36bn private investment in Bangladesh
summary: The investment, totaling 1 trillion yen, will be spread over the next five years, focusing on manufacturing and energy facilities.
details: Japan will agree to arrange 1 trillion yen ($6.36 billion) in private-sector investments in Bangladesh over the next five years, according to the Nikkei newspaper.
The arrangement will be mentioned in a joint statement following a summit between Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and her Bangladesh counterpart Tarique Rahman in Japan this month.
The investments are expected to be directed toward automobile and other manufacturing industries, as well as the construction of energy facilities.
The plan also involves companies entering the Bangladesh Special Economic Zone, which is being developed by parties including the Japanese trading house Sumitomo Corp.
caption:
Japan is set to invest $6.36 billion in Bangladesh over the next five years.

Japan will agree to arrange 1 trillion yen ($6.36 billion) in private-sector investments in Bangladesh over the next five years, according to the Nikkei newspaper.

The arrangement will be mentioned in a joint statement following a summit between Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and her Bangladesh counterpart Tarique Rahman in Japan this month.

The investments are expected to be directed toward automobile and other manufacturing industries, as well as the construction of energy facilities.

The plan also involves companies entering the Bangladesh Special Economic Zone, which is being developed by parties including the Japanese trading house Sumitomo Corp.
